## Nominal dimensions are a starting hypothesis

Printed dimensions depend on machine calibration, material, orientation, layer height, toolpath width, shrinkage, cooling, and feature shape. Internal holes and external pins may not deviate in the same way.

## Test the interface

Create a small coupon containing several clearances, hole diameters, or pin/socket pairs around the target dimension. Label each value in the model. Print with the intended printer, material, orientation, and profile; measure the result and choose a fit from evidence.

Functional choices include:

- free-running clearance for moving or removable parts;
- sliding fit for guided assembly;
- snug fit for repeatable location;
- press fit where material behaviour and removal requirements make it appropriate;
- pilot, clearance, counterbore, or captured-nut features for conventional fasteners.

## Useful applications

Brackets, adapters, knobs, guards, cable guides, tool holders, replacement spacers, drill guides, enclosures, and jigs are valuable when they solve a real measured problem. A repair part should be evaluated for load, temperature, impact, chemicals, UV, wear, and failure consequences before use.
